stories.title: Baltimore creates mental health crisis agency
stories.summary: The Baltimore City Council has established a Department of Neighborhood Safety to handle mental health crises and nonviolent emergencies. The agency will employ clinicians and peer responders, holding equal standing with the city's police and fire departments. A mental health call is now a departmental matter.

stories.title: Michigan eyes social media settlement for youth mental health
stories.summary: Michigan lawmakers plan to use at least $171 million from a settlement with Meta to bolster youth mental health efforts. The state alleged Meta intentionally designed addictive features that harmed young people. The funds are intended to address the safety concerns raised by the state attorney general.

stories.title: Researchers address non-optimal responders in PTSD treatment
stories.summary: The Road Home Program reports that 84 percent of veterans and active-duty members show improvement after PTSD treatment. Researchers are now focusing on the remaining 16 percent of participants who do not show similar progress. The goal is to ensure no veteran is left behind.

stories.title: Study links depression to lower employment in Indian adults
stories.summary: A study of 27,092 Indian adults aged 45 to 60 years found a clear link between depressive symptoms and a lower likelihood of employment. Researchers used the Composite International Diagnostic Interview to assess participants. As symptoms increase, the probability of working falls.

stories.title: Community care proposed as alternative to psychiatric hospitalization
stories.summary: A meta-analysis published in the Journal of the American Academy of Child and Adolescent Psychiatry suggests intensive community care services offer a promising alternative to inpatient treatment for adolescents. The services may reduce hospital admission days and improve psychosocial functioning compared to traditional inpatient care.

stories.title: New Jersey nonprofits offer free veteran mental health sessions
stories.summary: The New Jersey Reentry Corporation and the Steven A. Cohen Military Family Clinic have launched a partnership to provide 12 free mental health sessions to veterans. The initiative aims to support 250 individuals regardless of discharge status. The program began operations on October 1.

stories.title: Meditation linked to neuroactive drug pathways
stories.summary: An exploratory study in Frontiers in Human Neuroscience found that molecular signatures from meditation overlap with gene expression responses induced by over 438 pharmaceuticals. These compounds modulate the brain's excitation-inhibition balance. Meditation is frequently used as a non-pharmacological approach for managing stress.

stories.title: Yoga protocol shows cognitive benefits in randomized study
stories.summary: A randomized controlled study of 139 healthy adults in Pune found that a 45-day yoga protocol improved cognitive functions and neural connectivity. Participants were assessed using standardized tests and resting-state fMRI. The United Nations promotes the protocol for global participation.

stories.title: Queen Suthida to open Global Wellness Summit in Phuket
stories.summary: Queen Suthida is scheduled to preside over the opening of the 20th Global Wellness Summit in Phuket on November 11. The event runs for four days under the theme of the science, art and soul of wellness. Organisers expect 600 delegates to attend the anniversary summit.

stories.title: Atlanta police add Calm app to officer wellness resources
stories.summary: The Atlanta Police Department is providing officers with access to the Calm app to support stress management and emotional well-being. Funded by the Atlanta Police Foundation, the initiative aims to reinforce the message that taking care of oneself is part of taking care of others.

stories.title: New scoring system tracks sleep in advanced Parkinson's
stories.summary: A new sleep scoring system identifies disruptions in patients with advanced Parkinson's disease that standard methods often miss. The system tracks five sleep and wake stages linked to cognitive decline and motor fluctuations. It aims to help clinicians better identify and monitor severe sleep disturbances.

stories.title: Study links late-night habits to metabolic health
stories.summary: A study from UTHealth Houston found that adults with obesity who stay up and eat later may face higher risks of inflammation and metabolic disease. Researchers analyzed how circadian behaviors relate to health in adults. The findings were published in the journal iScience.

stories.title: Research suggests sleep and inflammation fuel each other
stories.summary: Scientists publishing in Aging Cell have concluded that poor sleep quality and inflammaging worsen each other in a cycle. The review suggests this relationship reduces quality of life and fuels age-related diseases. The findings were based on a review of existing literature on circadian dysregulation.

stories.title: Foundayo reduces sleep apnea breathing interruptions
stories.summary: Eli Lilly reported that its oral weight-loss drug Foundayo reduced breathing interruptions in obese adults with obstructive sleep apnea by 44% over 52 weeks. The study met its primary goal. The drug is intended for use in patients with moderate to severe forms of the disorder.

stories.title: Toddler sleep patterns linked to emotional regulation
stories.summary: Research published in the Journal of Activity, Sedentary and Sleep Behaviors suggests that longer nighttime sleep predicts better emotional self-regulation in toddlers six months later. Physical activity showed no such association. The study is the first to evaluate these temporal connections in this age group.

stories.title: Oral GLP-1 drug studied for sleep apnea
stories.summary: Clinical trials show that adults with excess weight and sleep apnea who took the oral drug orforglipron had 18 fewer breathing interruptions per hour after one year, compared to five for the placebo group. Participants also saw reductions in body weight and blood markers of inflammation.

stories.title: Sleep therapy study targets glymphatic markers
stories.summary: A clinical study reports that patient-controlled sleep therapy using dexmedetomidine is associated with increased glymphatic-related neuroimaging markers. The research focused on individuals with chronic insomnia comorbid with major depressive disorder. It aimed to determine if imaging could differentiate patient treatment sensitivity.

stories.title: Alzheimer's research tracks slow-wave sleep changes
stories.summary: Research published in Alzheimer's Research and Therapy indicates that sleep architecture progressively deteriorates across the Alzheimer's disease continuum. The study analyzed slow-wave activity using overnight polysomnography. Specific features of slow-wave sleep in cognitively unimpaired individuals were found to be associated with longitudinal cognitive performance.

stories.title: Sleep psychologist explains exhaustion without sleep
stories.summary: Sleep psychologist Dr. Alicia Roth says there are specific reasons why people can feel exhausted but struggle to fall asleep. The phenomenon involves understanding the difference between being tired and being sleepy. The full piece is for subscribers.

stories.title: Yoga-based rehab shows heart failure benefits
stories.summary: A study of 3,500 heart failure patients across 16 hospitals in India found that a yoga-based rehabilitation program improved exercise capacity and quality of life. The Yoga-CaRe program focused on patients with reduced ejection fraction. The results were published following the multi-hospital trial.

stories.title: Jane Fonda shifts to gentle exercise routine
stories.summary: Jane Fonda, 88, has transitioned from high-intensity aerobics to a routine focused on walking, strength, and flexibility. Fonda told People that she continues to exercise daily but at a slower pace. Health experts suggest such routines are sustainable for maintaining strength as individuals age.

stories.title: Calf raises touted for circulation benefits
stories.summary: Experts suggest that regular calf raises may help improve circulation by pumping blood from the lower legs toward the heart. The calf muscles are sometimes described as a second heart due to their role in venous return. The movement is recommended as a simple daily exercise.

stories.title: Yoga-based rehab linked to improved quality of life
stories.summary: A study found that yoga-based cardiac rehabilitation improved the quality of life for people living with heart failure. The research, as reported by Medical Xpress, highlights the potential benefits of integrating yoga into cardiac care programs. Further details are available in the full report.

stories.title: Vanessa Feltz discusses post-weight loss habits
stories.summary: Broadcaster Vanessa Feltz has spoken about her experience with weight loss and the use of weight-loss drugs under medical supervision. She noted the importance of building strength through walking and weight training. The full interview is available via MailOnline.

stories.title: Exercise linked to increased irisin levels
stories.summary: A meta-analysis of 50 randomized controlled trials found that regular exercise significantly increases levels of irisin, a molecule released by muscles. The boost in irisin was associated with improvements in metabolic health markers in adults with overweight or obesity. The study highlights how exercise rewires metabolism.

stories.title: Standing exercises for hamstring strength
stories.summary: A report suggests five standing exercises that may restore hamstring strength in adults over 65 more effectively than walking. The exercises are intended to support mobility and physical health. The full article is available on the Eat This Not That website.

stories.title: Exercise regimen shows promise for geriatric depression
stories.summary: Older adults in a structured eight-week trial combining aerobic and resistance training saw a greater reduction in depressive symptoms than peers on standard antidepressants. The study of thirty-two participants in Islamabad suggests physical conditioning may impact mental health outcomes. The results remain limited to a small outpatient group.

stories.title: Yoga ranked top for sleep improvement in meta-analysis
stories.summary: Researchers at Harbin Sport University pooled 30 trials involving 2,500 adults to compare exercise types for sleep disturbances. Yoga was ranked first for improving sleep quality. The authors of the study, published in Sleep and Biological Rhythms, urge caution regarding the findings due to the varied trial data.

stories.title: Kimchi-derived probiotic shows effects in mouse study
stories.summary: Researchers found that a lactic acid bacteria strain isolated from kimchi, HY7715, reduced aging toxins in lab mice over eight weeks. The findings, published in the Journal of Microbiology and Biotechnology, suggest potential effects on brain and gut tissues. The study was conducted on artificially aged mice.

stories.title: UCSF study tracks dopamine pathway in food preference
stories.summary: UCSF researchers identified a dopamine circuit in mice that links food flavors to nutrient intake. Human imaging showed similar responses in the amygdala, though the study did not test clinical applications. The research offers clues into how the brain learns to associate specific flavors with caloric value.

stories.title: Chaka Khan opens vegan cafe in Georgia
stories.summary: Grammy-winning artist Chaka Khan has partnered with her sister and chef Anne Onyeneho to open Chaka’s Plantbaed Café in Serenbe, Georgia. The menu features plant-based offerings including tacos and bowls. It serves as a sister location to a cafe opened in Vinings in 2024.

stories.title: Study links moderate coffee consumption to lower anxiety
stories.summary: A 13-year study of 460,000 UK Biobank participants found that moderate coffee drinkers were the least likely to develop anxiety and depression. Researchers identified a potential sweet spot for mood benefits. The study suggests the relationship between caffeine and the nervous system is more complex than previously assumed.

stories.title: Plant-based dairy alternatives may lack iodine
stories.summary: A UK modeling study suggests that replacing dairy with plant-based alternatives could increase iodine shortfalls, particularly in teenage girls and young women. Most plant-based milks and yogurts contain little iodine, a mineral used for thyroid hormones. The model tested adding iodine as a potential fix for the deficiency.

stories.title: Gut bacteria may consume intestinal lining when fiber is low
stories.summary: Scientists found that gut bacteria can feed on the protective mucus lining of the intestines when fiber is scarce. This process produces potentially harmful compounds. The research suggests that fiber and certain plant proteins help regulate this bacterial activity, which may explain benefits associated with plant-based diets.

stories.summary: Interest in healthy aging is reaching beyond the doctor’s office. McKinsey’s 2025 consumer research reports growing demand for longevity products and services. stories.title: NAD levels found stable with age in study
stories.summary: A study of 1,000 people published in Nature Metabolism found that blood NAD levels do not decline with age in healthy participants. The findings challenge a core assumption behind the NAD supplement market. Levels were found to be lower in people with hypertension, though the causality remains unclear.

stories.title: ATTR-CM Patients Prioritize Longevity and Enjoyable Activities Over Basic
stories.summary: A multinational study published in Cardiology and Therapy reveals that individuals living with transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) prioritize treatments that extend their lives and allow them to continue engaging in meaningful activities, often valuing these outcomes over basic self-care routines. The research, conducted through a

stories.title: Healf identifies 2027 wellness trends
stories.summary: Wellness retailer Healf forecasts hormone health, male fertility, and personalised longevity as key consumer trends for 2027. The report, based on purchase data from one million UK customers, suggests shoppers are buying fewer, more targeted products. The company claims this shift is informed by better personal health data.

stories.title: Estée Lauder launches skin longevity platform
stories.summary: Estée Lauder has unveiled a breakthrough scientific platform to advance the next era of skin science. The company claims it will focus on master regulators of skin longevity by targeting interconnected biological pathways. The platform serves as a foundation for brands including Clinique and The Ordinary. Science is now a

stories.title: Study links lifetime oestrogen to longevity
stories.summary: A study of 112,381 postmenopausal women suggests higher lifetime oestrogen exposure decelerates biological aging and extends life expectancy. Researchers tracked reproductive indices across UK and US cohorts to evaluate how hormonal milestones affect survival. The findings offer insights into female endocrine aging and preventive health.

stories.title: Review explores acupuncture and gut immunity
stories.summary: A narrative review in Immunity, Inflammation and Disease suggests acupuncture may modulate host immunity through the gut microbiota-macrophage axis. The authors propose the practice functions as an eco-immunological therapy by recalibrating microbial networks. They note the hypothesis requires further causal validation. The review is a synthesis of existing literature.

stories.title: Allendale Acupuncture and Wellness offers pain relief
stories.summary: Allendale Acupuncture and Wellness is promoting its services for chronic pain and neuropathy. The clinic highlights a patient story involving reduced discomfort and improved quality of life. This piece is sponsored content and does not reflect the views of the publisher. Relief is a matter of perspective.

stories.title: Research examines electroacupuncture for knee pain
stories.summary: A multicentre randomized trial compared electroacupuncture with sham acupuncture for knee osteoarthritis. The study assessed clinical outcomes and MRI measures following a six-week course of treatment. The author notes that effective work requires reading the whole picture, including hormone data, sleep, and digestion. Results are described as encouraging.

stories.title: Integrative medicine for cancer symptom management
stories.summary: Integrative medicine combines Western cancer treatments with complementary therapies to address symptoms like pain and insomnia. Oncology nurses are encouraged to consider acupuncture and massage to improve patient care. The field aims to establish an evidence base for interventions beyond standard clinical practice. Symptoms remain a focus.

stories.title: Gene variants may influence acupuncture response
stories.summary: A secondary analysis of a randomized trial suggests specific gene variants in HTR3A and COMT may correlate with patient responses to electroacupuncture for chemotherapy-induced nausea. The study focused on breast cancer patients to see if genetics predict protection against vomiting. Results differed significantly across specific genotypes.

stories.title: Review evaluates acupuncture for mitochondrial repair
stories.summary: A review in the journal Chinese Medicine evaluates preclinical evidence for acupuncture regulating mitochondrial homeostasis after traumatic brain injury. The authors distinguish between direct and indirect evidence, concluding that mechanisms require further validation. Direct evidence specific to brain injury remains limited. The review suggests potential, pending more research.

stories.title: AIIA concludes Saushrutam 2026 seminar
stories.summary: The All India Institute of Ayurveda has concluded its three-day international seminar, Saushrutam 2026. The institute also renewed its memorandum of understanding with IIT Delhi. The event focused on international collaboration in the field. The full details of the agreement were not disclosed.

stories.title: Tulah Clinical Wellness Sanctuary opens in India
stories.summary: Tulah Clinical Wellness Sanctuary is a new luxury retreat in India featuring on-site doctors and 30 acres of gardens. The facility combines Western medical technology with traditional holistic healing systems. Guests follow daily routines guided by multilingual staff. The sanctuary offers a roster of complimentary activities for visitors.

stories.title: Annapurna Hostels hosts Diwali celebrations
stories.summary: Annapurna Hostels organized festive activities and decorations for residents during Diwali. The event aimed to provide a warm environment for students living away from their families. Students participated in music and decor to create a festive atmosphere. The hostel provided a space for communal celebration.

research.title: Scientists discover hidden brain changes linked to common sleep disorders
research.summary: Scientists have discovered that sleep disorders are associated with structural changes in brain regions that control attention, decision-making, and emotions, potentially explaining why disrupted sleep can affect everyday thinking and behavior. The findings, drawn from 57 brain imaging studies, reveal both shared and disorder-specific patterns that could lead.

research.summary: Scientists at UC San Francisco have developed a powerful new cancer therapy that remains inactive until it reaches the brain, where it switches on to attack deadly tumors.
